atemporal.name: Atemporal
atemporal.definition: A deterministic static object, equation/constraint solution, configuration, or set with no intrinsic model-time evolution or construction index. Its numerical computation method is separate.

discrete time.name: Discrete time
discrete time.definition: A deterministic discrete-index rule assigns a unique successor state or next construction stage. The index may be model time or intrinsic construction depth; an arbitrary numerical loop used only to solve/render a static object is not itself a generator. A stochastic initial condition does not alter the deterministic law class.

continuous time.name: Continuous time
continuous time.definition: A deterministic law specifies the state over a continuous model-time parameter. It may include endogenous collision events, switching, guard-triggered transitions, and resets; hybrid is a temporal attribute, not a substrate.

stochastic.name: Stochastic
stochastic.definition: Classify the specified generator law, not an arbitrary random initial sample, numerical seed, or visualization. A deterministic rule remains Discrete time or Continuous time when only its initial condition is sampled randomly; record that ensemble separately. Use Stochastic when probability is intrinsic to the specified generator: static random-object sampling, probabilistic transitions, stochastic forcing or coefficients, random event times, or a probabilistic construction law. A sampled environment becomes a deterministic fixed realization once held fixed, unless subsequent transitions remain probabilistic.

nondeterministic.name: Nondeterministic
nondeterministic.common: possibilistic: several open-branching next states, with no probabilities attached
nondeterministic.definition: Use only when the mathematical transition is genuinely relational/set-valued and neither a unique deterministic successor nor a probability distribution is specified. Record discrete, continuous, event-driven, or hybrid temporal structure separately. If a firing/update strategy resolves choices uniquely, use the corresponding deterministic class; if choices have probabilities, use Stochastic.

P.name: Abstract point-state space
P.common: a point in an abstract state space; not a spatial point cloud
P.definition: The native state is an abstract state-space element, tuple/vector, finite abstract state, or trajectory-valued stochastic process, not a spatial point set and not a population of individually represented physical entities. A finite-dimensional N-body formulation can be represented as one vector, but use E when per-body identities and individual states are the modeling carriers. The presence of several state variables alone does not imply X.

F.name: Continuum field
F.common: one or more fields over a continuous spatial domain
F.definition: The native state is a field over a continuum domain. Multiple components on the same field domain do not automatically make the substrate composite.

L.name: Lattice / fixed graph
L.common: values on fixed discrete sites or fixed-connectivity nodes
L.definition: State values or occupancies are attached to a fixed set of lattice sites, graph nodes, or Petri-net places with fixed support/connectivity. This includes cellular automata, spin systems, lattice gases, site-occupancy/exclusion processes, and fixed-graph interacting particle systems specified as site-state Markov processes. Use E when individually tracked mobile entities carry their own state; use R when the graph/edge/higher-order relationships themselves are state variables.

E.name: Entity
E.common: individually represented particles, agents, cells, or bodies
E.definition: Individually represented particles, agents, cells, organisms, or bodies are native carriers with per-entity state such as position, velocity, orientation, type, size, or lifecycle. Population size may be fixed or variable. Fixed N alone does not decide P versus E: use E when individual bodies and their per-body states are semantically modeled; use P when only an abstract state vector is the intended object; use L when only site occupancy/state on fixed sites is native and entity identity is not modeled.

R.name: Relational
R.common: relations, edges, or higher-order incidence are primary state variables
R.definition: The native object is a graph, hypergraph, incidence structure, relational system, or a set of relationships/edge weights/topology explicitly treated as variables. Static relational structures belong here too. Graph grammars are R when graph incidence is rewritten. Use S for symbolic strings, terms, and syntax; use G for geometric realization or unlabelled spatial set-valued outputs. A graph embedded in space remains R if connectivity is the defining object; record embedding as an attribute.

S.name: Symbolic / combinatorial
S.common: strings, trees, grammars, or other symbolic/combinatorial objects
S.definition: The native object is a symbolic expression, word/string, formal language, grammar, symbolic sequence, or combinatorial structure represented/manipulated as syntax or symbols. A graph, hypergraph, or tree viewed through explicit vertex/edge/incidence relations belongs in R; a tree used as a symbolic term or syntax tree can be S. A geometric realization—such as a tiling, curve, or shape—is G. The model’s native representation decides.

G.name: Geometric / set-valued
G.common: a spatial set, curve, surface, interface, tiling, or shape
G.definition: The primary object is a geometric/set-valued object: a point set without persistent identities, region, curve, surface, interface, tiling, partition, shape, packing, basin, or geometric realization. If individuals carry their own identities/attributes, use E; if the mathematical state is a scalar level-set or other continuum field whose zero/evolving level set represents the interface, use F. An interface-first free-boundary formulation with a quasi-static bulk field solved diagnostically can remain G; a dynamically evolving bulk field explicitly coupled to the interface can be X.

X.name: Composite substrate
X.common: two or more heterogeneous state carriers are explicitly coupled
X.definition: Use X only when two or more heterogeneous state carriers are independently represented and explicitly coupled, e.g. agents plus a continuum chemical field. Hybrid is a temporal/control attribute, not a substrate. A hybrid automaton often qualifies for X because its mathematical state combines discrete modes with continuous variables/clocks; a reduced or alternative state-vector representation may warrant P. Do not move all hybrid systems to X or P merely from the word “hybrid”. Several components of the same continuum field on the same domain remain F.

edition: v0.1.6 — square archetype correction pass and 7 additional mathematical renderers

audit_summary.source_audit: The pasted audit was evaluated claim-by-claim against the current v1.2 records and taxonomy definitions. Several findings were already fixed in v1.2; valid remaining corrections are applied in v1.4; overbroad proposed merges/reclassifications are qualified rather than accepted blindly.
audit_summary.policy_law: The law class describes the specified generator rule. Random initial data alone do not make a deterministic rule stochastic. Random construction of the network ensemble is S; a fixed sampled network realization can then have deterministic DΔ dynamics.
audit_summary.policy_substrate: P = abstract state-space process/vector; F = continuum field; L = values/occupancies on fixed sites/nodes; E = individually represented entities; R = relational/graph-incidence structure; C = symbolic syntax/strings/terms; G = geometric/set-valued output; X = explicitly coupled heterogeneous state carriers. Native representation, not appearance, decides.
audit_summary.duplicate_policy: Exact duplicates are redirected as aliases. Similar model names, reductions, families, parameter regimes, and alternate formulations are retained as separate records when their laws or specification levels differ; links do not imply equivalence unless stated.
audit_summary.record_levels: Generator laws, static outputs, particular solutions, parameter regimes, numerical methods, solvers, and renderers are explicitly distinguished. A method is not a physical generator, but its underlying event/rate law may still be a generator when fully specified.
audit_summary.thumbnail_method: REPEATABLE RECORD-LEVEL PROCEDURE: (1) choose the canonical record, not its alias, parent family, method, or renderer; (2) confirm the actual formal model and a source for its rule/equation; (3) specify a single bounded archetype, including equations/transition table, parameters, initialization, boundary conditions, seed, discretization, number of updates/iterations and display window; (4) implement that exact law in a named Python renderer; (5) render the computed state/object into a square 236×236 working image and downsample to a 118×118 asset; (6) use the fixed thin-line/paper/black/grey/midpoint palette without inventing structural details; (7) record source URL, rule, parameters, RNG seed, renderer and rationale; (8) inspect full-size cases and a contact sheet; (9) compare against active thumbnails and sub-record relationships; (10) leave a record visibly pending if the image is schematic, the equation is under-specified, the renderer does not actually implement the rule, or the result is not recognizable. Reference images are for finding the canonical visual signature, not for tracing; do not mirror or rotate source images.
audit_summary.stage: v0.1.6. Fourteen previously generated archetypes were recomputed from their bounded mathematical specifications, and seven additional record-specific archetypes were added. All other images remain withheld pending their own source/math/renderer audit.
audit_summary.unresolved: This is a curated working taxonomy. This release is not a claim of independent primary-source verification of all records, nor proof that a finite list exhausts every eligible mathematical generator.
audit_summary.alias_policy: Exact same specified generator labels are retained only as marked non-primary alias redirects to one canonical identity. Closely related families, special cases, limits, reductions, formulations and output objects remain separate when the mathematical law or identity differs; links do not assert equivalence.
audit_summary.source_policy: New Part 2 entries include source_refs and the source shelf records for the named model definitions. A few specialized thumbnail procedures are explicitly schematic when exact-law sampling is not implemented (notably the Arak polygonal Markov field).
audit_summary.known_limits: This catalog is a working, growing map, not a proof of mathematical exhaustiveness and not a claim that every historical record has had a primary-source review. All Part 2 entries are source-grounded at family-definition level, but exact parameters/versions must be specified for each reproducible instance.
audit_summary.thumbnail_specificity: v0.1.6 batch 2: 21 specific mathematical renderers (14 revised images and 7 additional records). All output assets are square 118×118 PNGs generated from equations, recurrence/CA rules, geometric constructions, or explicitly stated seeded stochastic realizations. The source verifies the law/standard visual identity; no web-image pixels are copied or traced. A reference image is never a substitute for implementing the rule.
audit_summary.primary_thumbnail_uniqueness: 29 active primary thumbnails have individually addressed assets; exact decoded-pixel duplicate check is performed for all active assets during build. Distinct file hashes alone do not certify semantic distinctness.
audit_summary.thumbnail_policy: HARD RULE: no thumbnail is marked authenticated solely because it renders, is unique, or is family-shaped. Only record-specific outputs whose underlying rule and conditions are recorded and whose visual identity is reviewed are displayed. All unprocessed legacy images are withheld.
audit_summary.filter_policy: All five filter dimensions (law, substrate, family, subtype/mechanism class, record_type) are derived from canonical records. Every selector’s available values/counts are recomputed from the intersection of the current search and all other selected dimensions; current incompatible selections are retained with zero counts so users can clear them. The interface does not maintain a separate hand-written filter vocabulary.

quality_checks.semantic_filter_mapping_independently_ve: NO — required next audit stage; schema validation is not semantic proof.

hard_rules: HARD RULE — FIVE-DIMENSION MAPPING: EVERY CANONICAL ENTRY MUST HAVE ACCURATE VALUES FOR LAW ARCHITECTURE, SUBSTRATE, MECHANISM FAMILY, MECHANISM CLASS/SUBTYPE, AND RECORD TYPE FROM THE SAME CANONICAL DATA. ANY SELECTION OR MIXED FILTER COMBINATION MUST INSTANTLY SHOW THE EXACT INTERSECTION; EACH FILTER’S OPTIONS/COUNTS MUST BE RECOMPUTED AGAINST THE OTHER ACTIVE SELECTIONS. NO MISSING OR HAND-WRITTEN DESYNCHRONIZED VALUES.

HARD RULE — ARCHETYPAL MATHEMATICAL VISUAL: EVERY DISPLAYED IMAGE MUST BE A RECOGNIZABLE, RECORD-SPECIFIC REPRESENTATION GENERATED FROM THE ACTUAL EQUATION, TRANSITION RULE, OR GEOMETRIC/COMBINATORIAL CONSTRUCTION OF THAT RECORD, OR FROM AN EXPLICITLY BOUNDED, SOURCE-REFERENCED FORMULATION. DO NOT SUBSTITUTE A GENERIC FAMILY ICON, A DIFFERENT MODEL, OR A RANDOM DECORATION. IF NOT VERIFIED, WITHHOLD THE IMAGE AND DISPLAY AUTHENTIC ARCHETYPE PENDING.

HARD RULE — REPRODUCIBILITY: STORE THE EQUATION/RULE, FORMULATION, PARAMETERS, INITIAL STATE, BOUNDARY CONDITIONS, FORCING, RNG SEED IF STOCHASTIC, DISCRETIZATION/NUMERICAL METHOD, RUN LENGTH, RENDERER ID, ALT TEXT, AND SOURCE REFERENCES FOR EVERY COMPUTED ARCHETYPE.

HARD RULE — UNIQUENESS: START WITH SPECIFIC NAMED INSTANCES; NEVER REUSE A SUB-RECORD/SUB-INSTANCE IMAGE FOR ITS PARENT OR ANOTHER RECORD. DO NOT ACCEPT DUPLICATE IMAGES MERELY BECAUSE THEIR FILE NAMES OR HASHES DIFFER. Exact mathematical duplicates must become alias redirects; distinct formulations and regimes stay separate when their laws differ.

HARD RULE — SQUARE CELL: EVERY PRIMARY VISUAL-GLOSSARY THUMBNAIL AND EVERY EXPANDED-RECORD THUMBNAIL MUST BE SQUARE. Working source and displayed thumbnail images are 1:1 (118×118 asset, 59×59 display), with a consistent one-pixel card border and inset; no record uses a widescreen image cell.

HARD RULE — NO WEB-IMAGE TRACING: CONSULT REFERENCES TO IDENTIFY A MODEL’S DEFINING LAW AND CANONICAL VISUAL SIGNATURE, THEN RECOMPUTE A NEW IMAGE FROM THAT LAW. NEVER TRACE, MIRROR, ROTATE, OR COSMETICALLY ALTER A WEB IMAGE. Do not claim copyright safety simply because the image was transformed.

HARD RULE — COMMON VISUAL GRAMMAR: USE PAPER #FFFEF9, BLACK #17191B, GREY #AEB4BA, AND OPTIONAL MIDPOINT #63676B; use thin lines and sharp borders. Mathematics and recognition take precedence over decoration.
audit_summary.visual_palette: Paper #FFFEF9, black #17191B, grey #AEB4BA, optional midpoint #63676B. All active thumbnails are square 118×118 PNG assets, displayed at 59×59 in the GUI.
audit_summary.source_provenance: For the v0.1.6 batch, source links document the equation/rule and canonical identity. Each displayed image is generated anew from the recorded mathematics. No web-image asset is used as a pixel source. Source citations do not certify that the entire legacy catalog is individually verified.
